smt-2021-general-01.title: Three cases
smt-2021-general-01.body:
If $30^\circ$ and $x^\circ$ are the two equal base angles, $x=30$. If $30^\circ$ is the apex angle, the base angles are $75^\circ$ each, so $x=75$. If $x^\circ$ is the apex angle and $30^\circ$ a base angle, $x=180-60=120$. The sum is $30+75+120=225$.

**Answer: 225**

smt-2021-general-02.title: Complementary counting
smt-2021-general-02.body:
All paths: $\binom84=70$ (4 right and 4 up moves). Paths through $(3,3)$: $\binom42\cdot\binom42=36$. So $70-36=34$.

**Answer: 34**

smt-2021-general-03.title: Square the semi-perimeter
smt-2021-general-03.body:
With sides $l,w$: $l^2+w^2=289$ and $lw=120$. Then $(l+w)^2=289+240=529=23^2$, so $l+w=23$ and the perimeter is $46$.

**Answer: 46 units**

smt-2021-general-04.title: Compare volumes
smt-2021-general-04.body:
The 3D-fier extends by a length $s$ (the cube has height $s$), so the cylinder has height $s$ and volume $\pi r^2 s$. The cube has volume $s^3$. So $\pi r^2s=5s^3$, hence $\frac{r^2}{s^2}=\frac5\pi$ and $\frac rs=\sqrt{\frac5\pi}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{5/\pi}$**

smt-2021-general-05.title: Relative heights
smt-2021-general-05.body:
Adding a penny to $99$ stacks changes the differences between stacks exactly as removing a penny from the one remaining stack. So we need to lower stacks to the height of the smallest, which requires removing $0+1+\cdots+99=4950$ pennies, one per move. Hence $4950$ moves.

**Answer: 4950**

smt-2021-general-05.title: Count skips
smt-2021-general-05.body:
After $n$ moves let stack $i$ have been skipped $s_i$ times, so $\sum s_i=n$ and its height is $i+n-s_i$. Equal heights force $s_{i+1}=s_i+1$, so $s_i=s_1+i-1\ge i-1$ and $n=\sum s_i\ge0+1+\cdots+99=4950$, with equality for $s_1=0$.

**Answer: 4950**

smt-2021-general-07.title: Similar triangles
smt-2021-general-07.body:
Triangle $ABE$ has a right angle at $B$ ($E$ is on line $BC$), with altitude $BF=\frac{12}5$ to the hypotenuse $AE$. In right triangle $ABF$ the hypotenuse is $AB=3$ and a leg is $\frac{12}5$, so $AF=\frac95$ and it is similar to a $3$-$4$-$5$ triangle. Triangle $AEB$ is similar to $ABF$ (shared angle at $A$), so $AB:BE:AE=3:4:5$, giving $AE=5$. The semicircle has radius $\frac52$ and area $\frac12\pi\cdot\frac{25}4=\frac{25\pi}8$.

**Answer: $\frac{25\pi}{8}$**

smt-2021-general-08.title: Legendre's formula
smt-2021-general-08.body:
The exponent of $7$ in $2020!$ is $\lfloor2020/7\rfloor+\lfloor2020/49\rfloor+\lfloor2020/343\rfloor=288+41+5=334$ (and $7^4=2401>2020$). So $7^{334}$ divides $2020!$ but $7^{335}$ does not.

**Answer: 335**

smt-2021-general-09.title: Each row is the first row or its complement
smt-2021-general-09.body:
Colour the first row arbitrarily: $2^8$ ways. Every other row must either equal the first row or be its exact complement (if it agreed with the first row somewhere, it would have to agree everywhere). Conversely, any two such rows are equal or complementary, so the condition holds for all pairs. That gives $2$ choices for each of the other $7$ rows: $2^8\cdot2^7=2^{15}=32768$.

**Answer: 32768**

smt-2021-general-10.title: Right angle at A
smt-2021-general-10.body:
$O$ is the centre of the circle and lies on chord $EF$, so $EF$ is a diameter and $\angle EAF=90^\circ$ (Thales). Thus $\angle BAC=90^\circ$. If $\angle ACB=x$ then $\angle ABC=5x$ and $90+x+5x=180$, so $x=15$ and $\angle ABC=75^\circ$.

**Answer: 75**

smt-2021-general-12.title: Angle bisector theorem twice
smt-2021-general-12.body:
From $A$: $\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac23$, so let $AB=2x$, $AC=3x$. From $C$: $\frac{BF}{FA}=\frac{CB}{CA}$, i.e. $\frac{2}{2x-2}=\frac{5}{3x}$. Then $6x=10x-10$, so $x=\frac52$ and $AC=\frac{15}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{15}{2}$**

smt-2021-general-13.title: Distance equations
smt-2021-general-13.body:
Let $T$ be the driving time (in hours) that would get you there exactly at 8:00. Then $d=50\left(T-\frac15\right)=40\left(T+\frac14\right)$. So $50T-10=40T+10$, giving $T=2$ and $d=40\cdot2.25=90$ miles. Check: at $50$ mph it takes $1.8$ h, at $40$ mph $2.25$ h, and the difference is $0.45$ h $=27$ minutes ($12+15$). 

**Answer: 90 miles**

smt-2021-general-14.title: Vandermonde
smt-2021-general-14.body:
For one game, choose $k\ge1$ players from each of the two grades: $\sum_{k=1}^5\binom5k^2=\binom{10}5-1=251$ (using $\sum_k\binom5k^2=\binom{10}{5}$). The two games are independent, so the total is $251^2=63001$.

**Answer: 63001**

smt-2021-general-15.title: Ratio of counts
smt-2021-general-15.body:
$p=\frac{\#\text{Friday 13ths}}{\#\text{Fridays}}$ and $q=\frac{\#\text{Friday 13ths}}{\#\text{13ths}}$ (there is at least one Friday the 13th: August 13, 2021). So $\frac pq=\frac{\#\text{13ths}}{\#\text{Fridays}}=\frac{12}{53}$, because 2021 (365 days starting on a Friday) has $53$ Fridays.

**Answer: $\frac{12}{53}$**

smt-2021-general-16.title: Split by the absolute value
smt-2021-general-16.body:
For $x>1$ the inequality is $\frac1x-\frac1{x-1}>\frac1{x-2}$, i.e. $\frac{2-x^2}{x(x-1)(x-2)}>0$ which on $x>1$ holds for $\sqrt2<x<2$ (length $2-\sqrt2$).

For $x<1$ it is $\frac1x+\frac1{x-1}>\frac1{x-2}$, i.e. $\frac{x^2-4x+2}{x(x-1)(x-2)}>0$, which on $x<1$ holds for $0<x<2-\sqrt2$ (length $2-\sqrt2$).

The total length is $2(2-\sqrt2)=4-2\sqrt2$ (confirmed numerically).

**Answer: $4-2\sqrt2$**

smt-2021-general-17.title: Glue a 30-60-90 and a 45-45-90 triangle
smt-2021-general-17.body:
Place a $45$-$45$-$90$ triangle (legs $1$) next to a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle (sides $1,\sqrt3,2$) along a common side of length $1$ so that the angles at the common vertex add to $105^\circ$ ($45^\circ+60^\circ$) between sides $\sqrt2$ and $2$. By SAS this is triangle $ABC$. Then $BC=\sqrt3+1$ and $\angle ACB=45^\circ$. In right triangle $CAD$ with $\angle C=45^\circ$ and $AC=\sqrt2$: $CD=2$. Hence $BD=BC-CD=\sqrt3-1$.

**Answer: $\sqrt3-1$**

smt-2021-general-17.title: Law of cosines
smt-2021-general-17.body:
$BC^2=4+2-2\cdot2\cdot\sqrt2\cos105^\circ=6-\sqrt2(\sqrt2-\sqrt6)=4+2\sqrt3=(\sqrt3+1)^2$, so $BC=\sqrt3+1$. By the law of sines $\sin C=\frac{2\sin105^\circ}{BC}=\frac{(\sqrt6+\sqrt2)/2}{\sqrt3+1}=\frac{\sqrt2}2$, so $C=45^\circ$. In right triangle $CAD$, $CD=\frac{AC}{\cos45^\circ}=2$. So $BD=\sqrt3+1-2=\sqrt3-1$.

**Answer: $\sqrt3-1$**

smt-2021-general-18.title: Inclusion-exclusion
smt-2021-general-18.body:
Total arrangements: $8!=40320$. Couple 1 adjacent: $7!\cdot2=10080$; same for couple 2. Both adjacent: $6!\cdot2\cdot2=2880$. So the number with neither adjacent is $40320-2\cdot10080+2880=23040$.

**Answer: 23040**

smt-2021-general-19.title: Find three values
smt-2021-general-19.body:
Put $y=1$: $f(x+1)=f(x)f(1)+f(x+1)$, so $f(x)f(1)=0$ for all $x$; since $f(0)\ne0$, $f(1)=0$. Put $x=y=0$: $f(1)=f(0)^2+f(0)$, so $f(0)=-1$. Put $x=-1,y=2$: $f(-1)=f(-1)f(2)+f(1)$, so $f(-1)(1-f(2))=0$.

If $f(2)=1$ then $f$ passes through $(0,-1),(1,0),(2,1)$, so $f(x)=x-1$, not quadratic. So $f(-1)=0$ and $f$ passes through $(0,-1),(1,0),(-1,0)$: $f(x)=x^2-1$. (It satisfies the equation: both sides equal $x^2y^2+2xy$.) Therefore $f(3)=8$.

**Answer: 8**

smt-2021-general-20.title: Exponentiate
smt-2021-general-20.body:
The logarithm equation says $k^2(x+y)^2=xy$. Since $(x+y)^2=x^2+y^2+2xy=49xy$, we get $49k^2xy=xy$, so $k=\frac17$ (positive since the logarithms must be defined).

**Answer: $\frac17$**

smt-2021-general-21.title: Find the radii
smt-2021-general-21.body:
Two tangent spheres with radii $r_1,r_2$ have centres $r_1+r_2$ apart horizontally, and their top points differ in height by $|r_1-r_2|$. So the distance between the top points is $\sqrt{(r_1+r_2)^2+(r_1-r_2)^2}=\sqrt{2r_1^2+2r_2^2}$. With the three sides: $2r_1^2+2r_2^2=100$, $2r_2^2+2r_3^2=676$, $2r_3^2+2r_1^2=580$. So $r_1^2+r_2^2=50$, $r_2^2+r_3^2=338$, $r_3^2+r_1^2=290$; adding gives sum $339$, so $r_1^2=1$, $r_2^2=49$, $r_3^2=289$: radii $1,7,17$.

The centres form a triangle with sides $r_1+r_2=8$, $r_2+r_3=24$, $r_3+r_1=18$. Heron with $s=25$: area $=\sqrt{25\cdot17\cdot1\cdot7}=5\sqrt{119}$.

**Answer: $5\sqrt{119}$**

smt-2021-general-22.title: Chinese remainder theorem
smt-2021-general-22.body:
Let $N$ be the number of students. $N\equiv1\equiv-4\pmod5$ and $N\equiv5\equiv-4\pmod9$, so $N\equiv-4\pmod{45}$. Also $N\equiv4\equiv-3\pmod7$ and $N\equiv10\equiv-3\pmod{13}$, so $N\equiv-3\pmod{91}$.

Write $N=91k-3$. Then $91k-3\equiv-4\pmod{45}$ gives $k\equiv-1\pmod{45}$, so the smallest positive $k$ is $44$ and $N=91\cdot44-3=4001$.

**Answer: 4001**
